# Your Environment {#chp:env}

Code runs somewhere: on some operating system, with some options set, and
some environment variables defined. This chapter helps you read that
environment and change it temporarily without leaving a mess.

## Options and environment variables {#sec:grp-env-vars}

Configure behavior from the outside, and put things back afterward.

### Let an option fall back to an environment variable {#sec:env-option}

Package authors often want users to configure behavior either with
`options()` in `.Rprofile`, or with an environment variable in `.Renviron`.
`env_option()` checks `options()` first, then looks for an environment variable
named `R_<NAME>` (uppercased, dots turned into underscores):

```{r}
Sys.setenv(R_XFUN_TEST_OPTION = "from-env")
env_option("xfun.test.option")     # "from-env"

options(xfun.test.option = TRUE)
env_option("xfun.test.option")     # TRUE: options() wins
options(xfun.test.option = NULL)   # reset
env_option("xfun.test.option")     # "from-env" again
Sys.unsetenv("R_XFUN_TEST_OPTION")
```

### Set an environment variable for a while {#sec:set-envvar}

`set_envvar()` sets variables and returns their previous values, so you can put
things back when you are done:

```{r}
old = set_envvar(c(MY_TOKEN = "secret"))
Sys.getenv("MY_TOKEN")
set_envvar(old)  # restore
Sys.getenv("MY_TOKEN")
```

## The system and the session {#sec:grp-env-system}

Know where code runs, and run parts of it only once.

### Know which OS you are on {#sec:os}

The `is_*()` family tells you the current operating system, without parsing
`R.version` yourself:

```{r}
is_windows()
is_macos()
is_linux()
is_unix()   # TRUE on macOS and Linux
is_arm64()  # TRUE on Apple silicon
```

### Get a compact session summary {#sec:session-info}

When you report a bug, you want session info that is short and focused.
`session_info()` trims `sessionInfo()`: no base-package noise, no BLAS details.
Give it a list of packages for a focused summary:

```{r}
session_info(c("xfun", "litedown"), dependencies = FALSE)
```

### Do something only once {#sec:do-once}

A deprecation message that prints on every call is annoying. `do_once()` runs
a task the first time and skips it afterward in the same R session:

```{r}
for (i in 1:3) {
  do_once(message("This prints once."), "my-one-time-task")
}
```
